text:
Background: MWC needs L = [free enzyme in I] / [free enzyme in A], so the derivation must know which form is the free enzyme that switches conformation. A form with no bound metabolite and no residual is free. Every enumerated mechanism has exactly one (E), so nothing changes for them. Hand-written ones can have two, for example Cleland's iso uni-uni: E + S ⇌ E(S), E(S) <--> F + P, F <--> E.

Today: each conformation is normalized by the first free form in species order, chosen separately in each state after pruning. That can be E in the active state and F in the inactive one: 1–5% errors in one hand-built case and NaN (0 ^ 2 in the printed law) in another.

Recommended: one flip form per allosteric mechanism, chosen by a fixed content rule (for example the free form of conformation E). A second free form is allowed only inside the flip form's rapid-equilibrium segment, where moving the flip only rescales L. Anywhere else (across a ping-pong, or a steady-state isomerization that carries flux) moving the flip changes the law by 12–45%, so the constructor rejects the mechanism with a message.

Alternative: the DSL names the flip form, and the user decides.
